iterative_source_discovery_summary.final_coverage_assessment: Coverage is partial. The single confirmed in-window aggregate is the WHO Multi-Country Sitrep #22 (who.int), which reports 10,556 cholera cases and 162 deaths in Haiti from 1 January to 29 December 2024 — a full-year figure that encompasses but does not isolate Q4 2024 (October–December). A newly surfaced PAHO document dated "4 Octobre 2024" (phsa-haiti-update-oct2024.pdf) is the most promising Q4-specific candidate, as its title date falls within the window; however, its snippet does not contain explicit Q4 case/death counts — only contextual narrative about the humanitarian crisis and cholera as a listed health threat. No MSPP weekly bulletins for epi weeks 40–52/2024 were surfaced. No UNICEF Q4 2024 humanitarian situation reports were retrieved. No ProMED Q4 2024 alerts appeared. No subnational (département-level) Q4 2024 data was confirmed in any snippet. The PAHO French-language sitreps retrieved are from 2025 (epi weeks 35 and 47 of 2025), not Q4 2024. The ReliefWeb result is from 2014. The HAL.science result is a global cholera review, not a Haiti Q4 2024 primary source. Coverage of the target fields is therefore: disease ✓, country ✓, date_reported (partial — full-year 2024 only), cases_unspecified ✓ (10,556 from WHO sitrep), deaths ✓ (162 from WHO sitrep), subnational_location ✗ (no Q4-specific departmental data confirmed), locality ✗, cases_confirmed ✗ (Q4-specific), cases_suspected ✗ (Q4-specific), cases_probable ✗, hospitalizations ✗ (Q4-specific), source_url ✓ (WHO sitrep #22, PAHO Oct 2024 update), source_type ✓, evidence_quote (partial).
iterative_source_discovery_summary.final_trustworthiness_assessment: The WHO Multi-Country Sitrep #22 (who.int) is the highest-trust confirmed in-window source: official WHO document, explicitly dated covering through 29 December 2024, with a specific numeric figure (10,556 cases, 162 deaths). The PAHO October 2024 update (phsa-haiti-update-oct2024.pdf) is a high-trust candidate (paho.org domain, title date within Q4 2024) but its snippet does not confirm specific Q4 case/death counts — it must be treated as a candidate pending content verification. All other accepted results are either out-of-window (pre-Q4 2024 or 2025), off-topic (Malawi MoH), or insufficiently specific (global reviews, academic articles not covering Q4 2024 primary data). No circular reporting or aggregator-only sources were used as primary evidence. The 50% duplicate rate in iteration 2 (12/24 results) indicates search saturation for the query strategies used.
